notes: HomeStop = Shoppers Stop's Home vertical (categoryPath1=Home) on shared shoppersstop.com. Access: direct HTTP fetch (ClaudeBot Allowed in robots.txt). Checked: (1) main nav/mega-menu (webCategories, threeLevelItems/bargains) and the Homestop CLP's full CMS component list (category-grid, hero-banners incl. 'Brighten Up Your Home' explore-banner, shop-by-budget, deals-card) - every link resolves to an ordinary department/category page (e.g. /home-living/c-1120) or a plain '*' search with a categoryPath1=Home filter; no nav item, banner, or widget is labelled New Arrivals/New In/Just In/Latest/What's New/Recently Added anywhere in the Home vertical. (2) Found one 'sort=new_arrivals' query parameter, but only on a single unrelated fashion-brand CTA ('intune', a non-Home brand landing link with a discount filter) - this is a generic sort option occasionally wired into a marketing CTA, not a distinct Home New Arrivals PLP, and it would return the entire brand catalog re-ordered (no bounded 'new' product set), so it fails the brief's 'genuine product listing representing new arrivals' test; not recorded as a row. (3) Inspected raw Unbxd product-document schema for categoryPath1=Home - it contains a 'new_arrival' field (Yes/No), which looked like the real signal, but sampled 500 products across Home and every other department (Women/Men/Kids/Beauty, 100 each): the value is always 'No' or null, never 'Yes', on any product checked; filtering on new_arrival Yes/true/1 returned 0 products site-wide - a dormant/unused catalog attribute, not an active merchandising tag driving any listing. (4) Unbxd facets for Home (categoryPath1/2/3, brand, pro_type, gender, pattern, discountPercent, offer, color_family, fabric, v_size, country_of_origin) include no New Arrivals facet. (5) Site's own search for 'new arrivals' returns a non-discriminating 321-result fallback with the generic homepage title (not a curated landing page, not proof of a real concept either way per the false-absence rule) - treated as unreliable, consistent with (1)-(4) showing no real nav/taxonomy entry point. (6) Brute-force checked guessed URLs /new-arrivals, /new-arrival, /new-in, /whats-new, /just-in, /latest-arrivals, /home-new-arrivals - all 404. (7) sitemap-landingpages.xml on api-ssl.shoppersstop.com (separate host) returned HTTP 503 twice - host outage, not a block (www.shoppersstop.com returned 200 throughout); could not cross-check against it, but (1)-(6) already converge on a clear absence. Conclusion: no genuine New Arrivals-type merchandising PLP exists for HomeStop/Home on shoppersstop.com.
